fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.text: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASDs) are a group of conditions that can occur in a person who is exposed to alcohol during gestation.

consciousness.text: Consciousness is being aware of something internal to one's self, or of states or objects in one's external environment.

large language models.text: A large language model (LLM) is an AI model trained on a vast amount of text for natural language processing tasks, especially language generation.

subjective experience.text: The subjective character of experience, also referred to as subjective experience, is the first-person aspect of conscious experience.

multiple myeloma.text: Multiple myeloma (MM), also known as plasma cell myeloma and simply myeloma, is a cancer of plasma cells, a type of white blood cell that normally produces antibodies.

minimal residual disease.text: Minimal residual disease (MRD), also known as molecular residual disease, or measurable residual disease, is the medical condition in which small number of cancer cells persist in a patient either during or after treatme

gastric cancer.text: Stomach cancer, also known as gastric cancer, is a malignant tumor of the stomach.

gastroscopy.text: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) or oesophagogastroduodenoscopy (OGD), also called by various other names, is a diagnostic endoscopic procedure that visualizes the upper part of the gastrointestinal tract down to the duodenum.

gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.text: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) or gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) is a chronic upper gastrointestinal disease in which stomach content persistently and regularly flows up into the esophagus, resulting in symptoms and/or complications.

chronic inflammation.text: Inflammation is part of the biological defence response of body tissues.

red meat.text: In the context of nutrition, red meat is defined as meat obtained from mammals, including beef, pork, lamb/mutton, veal, and venison.

primary care.text: Primary care is the day-to-day healthcare given by a health care provider.

sea levels.text: Mean sea level is an average surface level of one or more among Earth's coastal bodies of water from which heights such as elevation may be measured.

coastal flooding.text: Coastal flooding occurs when dry and low-lying land is submerged (flooded) by seawater.

vaccination.text: Vaccination is the administration of a vaccine to help the immune system develop immunity from a disease.

haze.text: Haze is traditionally an atmospheric phenomenon in which dust, smoke, and other dry particulates suspended in air obscure visibility and the clarity of the sky.

indonesia.text: Indonesia, officially the Republic of Indonesia, is a country in Southeast Asia and Oceania, between the Indian and Pacific oceans.

social media.text: Social media are new media technologies that facilitate the creation, sharing and aggregation of content amongst virtual communities and networks.

agricultural communication.text: Agricultural communication, or agricultural communications, is a field that focuses on communication about agriculture-related information among agricultural stakeholders and between agricultural and non-agricultural sta

sustainable intensification.text: Intensive agriculture, also known as intensive farming, conventional, or industrial agriculture, is a type of agriculture, both of crop plants and of animals, with higher levels of input and output per unit of agricultural land area.

heat stress.text: Hyperthermia, also known as overheating, is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.

low- and middle-income countries.text: A developing country is a country with a less-developed industrial base and a lower Human Development Index (HDI) relative to developed countries.

placebo.text: A placebo is a medicine or treatment intended to appear genuine to its recipient, but which has no pharmaceutical effect.

excise tax.text: An excise, or excise tax, is any duty on a category of goods that is normally levied by a government at the moment of manufacture for domestic consumption.

price elasticity of demand.text: A good's price elasticity of demand is a measure of how sensitive the quantity demanded is to its price.

ultra-processed foods.text: Ultra-processed foods (UPF) are industrially manufactured food products, generally derived from natural food or synthesized from other organic compounds.

tax progressivity.text: A progressive tax is a tax in which the tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases.

metacognitive strategies.text: Metacognition is an awareness of one's thought processes and an understanding of the patterns behind them.

learning analytics.text: Learning analytics is the measurement, collection, analysis and reporting of data about learners and their contexts, for purposes of understanding and optimizing learning and the environments in which it occurs.

sexual dysfunction.text: Sexual dysfunction is difficulty experienced by an individual or partners during any stage of normal sexual activity, including physical pleasure, desire, preference, arousal, or orgasm.

influenza.text: Influenza, commonly known as the flu, is an infectious disease caused by influenza viruses.

population immunity.text: Herd immunity is a form of indirect protection that applies only to contagious diseases.

ezhip.text: EZH inhibitory protein is a protein that in humans is encoded by the gene EZHIP.

face perception.text: Facial perception is an individual's understanding and interpretation of the face.

zolpidem.text: Zolpidem, sold under the brand name Ambien among others, is a medication primarily used for the short-term treatment of sleeping problems.

opioids.text: Opioids are a class of drugs that derive from, or mimic, natural substances found in the opium poppy plant.

behavioral economics.text: Behavioral economics is the study of the psychological factors involved in the decisions of individuals or institutions, and how these decisions deviate from those implied by traditional economic theory.

carbon dioxide.text: Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2.

wheat cultivar.text: Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.

liver.text: The liver is a major metabolic organ exclusively found in vertebrates which performs many essential biological functions, such as detoxification of the organism and the synthesis of various proteins and other biochemicals necessary for digestion and growth.

metabolic dysfunction.text: Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).

vaping.text: An electronic cigarette (e-cigarette) or vape is a device that simulates tobacco smoking.

harm-reduction.text: Harm reduction, or harm minimization, refers to a range of intentional practices and public health policies designed to lessen the negative social and/or physical consequences associated with various human behaviors, both legal and illegal.

sweeteners.text: A sweetener is a substance added to food or drink to impart the flavor of sweetness, either because it contains a type of sugar, or because it contains a sweet-tasting sugar substitute.

gut bacteria.text: Gut microbiota, gut microbiome, or gut flora are the microorganisms, including bacteria, archaea, fungi, and viruses, that live in the digestive tracts of animals.

palaeolithic.text: The Paleolithic, or Old Stone Age, is a period in human prehistory distinguished by the original development of stone tools.

rock art.text: In archaeology, rock art refers to human-made markings placed on natural surfaces, typically vertical stone surfaces.

hunter-gatherers.text: A hunter-gatherer or forager is a human living in a community in which most or all food is obtained by procuring naturally occurring edible items from the local wildlife and vegetation via hunting, fishing and/or gatheri

fertility.text: Fertility in colloquial terms refers the ability to have offspring.

psychological resilience.text: Psychological resilience, or mental resilience, is the ability to cope mentally and emotionally with a crisis, or to return to pre-crisis status quickly.

mobile phone addiction.text: Problematic smartphone use is psychological or behavioral dependence on mobile phones.

deep brain stimulation.text: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a type of neurostimulation therapy in which an implantable pulse generator is surgically implanted below the skin of the chest and connected by leads to the brain to deliver controlled electrical impulses.

treatment-resistant depression.text: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) is often defined as major depressive disorder in which an affected person does not respond adequately to at least two different antidepressant medications at an adequate dose and for an adequate duration.

marketing strategy.text: Marketing strategy refers to the set of coordinated actions undertaken by an organization to increase sales, strengthen market presence, and achieve sustainable competitive advantage.

swot analysis.text: In strategic planning and strategic management, SWOT analysis is a decision-making technique that identifies the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of an organization or project.

loan officer.text: Loan officers evaluate, authorize, or recommend approval of loan applications for people and businesses.

learning management system.text: A Learning Management System (LMS) is a software application for the administration, documentation, tracking, reporting, automation, and delivery of educational courses, training programs, materials, or learning and development programs.

oral polio vaccine.text: Polio vaccine is a vaccine used to prevent poliomyelitis (polio).

essential tremor.text: Essential tremor (ET), also called benign tremor, familial tremor, and idiopathic tremor, is a medical condition characterized by involuntary rhythmic contractions and relaxations of certain muscle groups in one or more body parts of unknown cause.

thalamotomy.text: Thalamotomy is a surgical procedure in which a functional lesion is made into the thalamus to improve the overall brain function in patients.

lignin.text: Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.

gut microbiota.text: Gut microbiota, gut microbiome, or gut flora are the microorganisms, including bacteria, archaea, fungi, and viruses, that live in the digestive tracts of animals.

enterolignans.text: The lignans are a large group of low molecular weight polyphenols found in plants, particularly seeds, whole grains, and vegetables.

glp-1.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is a 30- or 31-amino-acid-long peptide hormone deriving from tissue-specific posttranslational processing of the proglucagon peptide.

indian ocean.text: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's five oceanic divisions, covering 70,560,000 km2 (27,240,000 sq mi) or approximately 20% of the water area of Earth's surface.

neuromodulation.text: Neuromodulation is the physiological process by which a given neuron uses one or more chemicals to regulate diverse populations of neurons.

electroconvulsive therapy.text: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a psychiatric treatment that causes a generalized seizure by passing electrical current through the brain.

drake equation.text: The Drake equation is a probabilistic argument used to estimate the number of active, communicative extraterrestrial civilizations in the Milky Way Galaxy.

santa ana winds.text: The Santa Ana winds, occasionally referred to as the devil winds, are strong, extremely dry katabatic winds that originate inland and affect coastal Southern California and northern Baja California.

prostate cancer.text: Prostate cancer is the uncontrolled growth of cells in the prostate, a gland in the male reproductive system below the bladder.

digital health.text: Digital health is a discipline that includes digital care programs, technologies with health, healthcare, living, and society to enhance the efficiency of healthcare delivery and to make medicine more personalized and precise.

supportive care.text: Symptomatic treatment, also called supportive care, supportive therapy, or palliative treatment, is any medical therapy of a disease that only affects its symptoms, not the underlying cause.

cataract.text: A cataract is a cloudy area in the lens of the eye that impairs vision.

nitrogen dioxide.text: Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.

pm2.5.text: Particulate matter (PM) or particulates are microscopic particles of solid or liquid matter suspended in the air.

cognitive appraisal.text: Cognitive appraisal is the subjective interpretation made by an individual to stimuli in the environment.

brain aging.text: Aging brain refers to biological and functional changes that occur in the brain as individuals advance in age.

levodopa.text: Levodopa, also known as L-DOPA, is a dopaminergic medication which is used in the treatment of Parkinson's disease (PD) and certain other conditions like dopamine-responsive dystonia and restless legs syndrome.

microbiota–gut–brain axis.text: The gut–brain axis, also described as gut–brain interaction, is the two-way biochemical signaling that takes place between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system (CNS).

medicaid.text: Medicaid is a government program in the United States that provides health insurance for adults and children with limited income and resources.

social insurance.text: Social insurance is a form of social welfare that provides insurance against economic risks.

pneumonia.text: Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.

randomized trial.text: In science, randomized experiments are the experiments that allow the greatest reliability and validity of statistical estimates of treatment effects.

observational study.text: In fields such as epidemiology, social sciences, psychology and statistics, an observational study draws conclusions without controlling the independent variable due to ethical or practical limitations.

genetic engineering.text: Genetic engineering, also called genetic modification or genetic manipulation, is the modification and manipulation of an organism's genes using technology.

synthetic biology.text: Synthetic biology (SynBio) is a multidisciplinary scientific field that applies the principles of engineering to develop new biological parts, devices, and systems or to redesign existing systems found in nature.

mitochondria.text: A mitochondrion is an organelle found in the cells of most eukaryotes, such as animals, plants and fungi.

human milk.text: Breast milk or mother's milk is milk produced by the mammary glands in the breasts of humans.

fibrosis.text: Fibrosis, also known as fibrotic scarring, is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.

metacognition.text: Metacognition is an awareness of one's thought processes and an understanding of the patterns behind them.

cognition.text: Cognition encompasses mental processes that deal with knowledge.

protoplanetary disk.text: A protoplanetary disk is a rotating circumstellar disc of dense gas and dust surrounding a young newly formed star, a T Tauri star, or Herbig Ae/Be star.

exoplanet.text: An exoplanet or extrasolar planet is a planet outside the Solar System.

obituary.text: An obituary is a biographical article written about someone who has recently died.

immunology.text: Immunology is a branch of biology and medicine that covers the study of immune systems in all organisms.

well-being.text: Well-being is what is intrinsically good for a person.

hypertension.text: Hypertension, also known as high blood pressure, is a long-term medical condition in which the blood pressure in the arteries is persistently elevated.

nerve fibers.text: A nerve is an enclosed, cable-like bundle of nerve fibers.

chemoimmunotherapy.text: Chemoimmunotherapy is chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy.

enceladus.text: Enceladus is the sixth-largest moon of Saturn and the 18th largest in the Solar System.

subsurface ocean.text: Planetary oceanography, also called astro-oceanography or exo-oceanography, is the study of oceans on planets and moons other than Earth.

orangutan.text: Orangutans are great apes native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia.

zero-emission.text: A zero emission engine, motor, process, or other energy source emits no waste products that pollute the environment or disrupt the climate.

belfast harbour.text: Belfast Harbour is a major maritime hub in Belfast, Northern Ireland, handling 67% of Northern Ireland's seaborne trade and about 25% of the maritime trade of the entire island of Ireland.

caenorhabditis elegans.text: Caenorhabditis elegans is a free-living transparent nematode about 1 mm in length that lives in temperate soil environments.

enteroendocrine cells.text: Enteroendocrine cells are specialized cells of the gastrointestinal tract and pancreas with endocrine function.

technology.text: Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.

physics.text: Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.

post-stroke depression.text: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a form of depression that may occur after a stroke.

convolutional neural networks.text: A convolutional neural network (CNN) is a type of feedforward neural network that learns features via filter optimization.

gilgamesh.text: Gilgamesh was a hero in ancient Mesopotamian mythology and the protagonist of the Epic of Gilgamesh, an epic poem written in Akkadian during the late 2nd millennium BC.

manichaeism.text: Manichaeism was a major world religion founded in the third century CE by the Parthian Iranian prophet Mani (216–274) in the Sasanian Empire.

deepfake.text: Deepfakes are images, videos, or audio that have been edited or generated using artificial intelligence, AI-based tools or audio-video editing software.

enso.text: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is a global climate phenomenon that emerges from variation in winds and sea surface temperatures over the tropical Pacific Ocean.

linguistic distance.text: Linguistic distance is the measure of how different one language is from another.

second language acquisition.text: Second-language acquisition (SLA), second-language learning or L2 acquisition, is the process of learning a language other than one's native language (L1).

deep neural networks.text: In machine learning, deep learning (DL) focuses on utilizing multilayered neural networks to perform tasks such as classification, regression, and representation learning.

color perception.text: Color vision (CV), a feature of visual perception, is an ability to perceive differences between light composed of different frequencies independently of light intensity.

contrastive learning.text: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is a paradigm in machine learning where a model is trained on a task using the data itself to generate supervisory signals, rather than relying on externally-provided labels.

limited english proficiency.text: Limited English proficiency (LEP) is a term used in the United States that refers to a person who is not fluent in the English language, often because it is not their native language.

epidural.text: Epidural administration is a method of medication administration in which a medicine is injected into the epidural space around the spinal cord.

spinal headache.text: Post-dural-puncture headache (PDPH) is a complication of puncture of the dura mater.

deep vein thrombosis.text: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a type of venous thrombosis involving the formation of a blood clot in a deep vein, most commonly in the legs or pelvis.

growth hormone.text: Growth hormone (GH) or somatotropin, also known as human growth hormone in its human form, is a peptide hormone that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration in humans and other animals.

deep sleep.text: Slow-wave sleep (SWS), often referred to as deep sleep, is the third stage of non-rapid eye movement sleep (NREM), where electroencephalography activity is characterised by slow delta waves.

latent space.text: A latent space, also known as a latent feature space or embedding space, is an embedding of a set of items within a manifold in which similar items are positioned closer to one another.

glp-1 receptor agonist.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, also known as GLP-1 agonists, GLP-1RAs, and informally as simply GLP-1s, are a class of medications that activate the GLP-1 receptor, causing reduced blood sugar, reduced appetite, and reduced energy intake.

major adverse cardiovascular events.text: Major adverse cardiovascular events is a composite endpoint frequently used in cardiovascular research.

fatty liver disease.text: Fatty liver disease (FLD), also known as hepatic steatosis and steatotic liver disease (SLD), is a condition where excess fat builds up in the liver.

gut health.text: Healthy digestion, also called digestive health, results in the absorption of nutrients from food without distressing symptoms.

animal models.text: A model organism is a non-human species that is extensively studied to understand particular biological phenomena, with the expectation that discoveries made in the model organism will provide insight into the workings of other organisms.

extreme weather.text: Extreme weather includes unexpected, unusual, severe, or unseasonal weather; weather at the extremes of the historical distribution—the range that has been seen in the past.

climate modeling.text: Numerical climate models are mathematical models that can simulate the interactions of important drivers of climate.

scientific publishing.text: Scientific literature encompasses a vast body of academic papers that spans various disciplines within the natural and social sciences.

retinitis pigmentosa.text: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a member of a group of genetic disorders called inherited retinal dystrophy (IRD) that cause loss of vision.

efficacy.text: Efficacy is the ability to perform a task to a satisfactory or expected degree.

starlink.text: Starlink Services, LLC is a telecommunications subsidiary of the American spaceflight company SpaceX, providing broadband Internet service in approximately 160 countries and territories.

satellite internet.text: Satellite Internet access is Internet access provided through communication satellites; if it can sustain high speeds, it is termed satellite broadband.

speed limits.text: Speed limits on road traffic, as used in most countries, set the legal maximum speed at which vehicles may travel on a given stretch of road.

thwaites glacier.text: Thwaites Glacier is an unusually broad and vast Antarctic glacier located east of Mount Murphy, on the Walgreen Coast of Marie Byrd Land.

computer model.text: Computer simulation is the running of a mathematical model on a computer, the model being designed to represent the behaviour of, or the outcome of, a real-world or physical system.

cardiothoracic surgery.text: Cardiothoracic (CT) surgery is the field of medicine involved in surgical treatment of organs inside the thoracic cavity — generally treatment of conditions of the heart, lungs, and other pleural or mediastinal structures.

epa.text: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is an independent agency of the United States government tasked with environmental protection matters.

heart valve replacement.text: Valve replacement is the surgical replacement of one or more of the heart valves with either an artificial heart valve or a bioprosthestic valve.

rabies.text: Rabies is a viral disease that causes inflammation of the brain in humans and other mammals.

post-exposure prophylaxis.text: Post-exposure prophylaxis, also known as post-exposure prevention (PEP), is any preventive medical treatment started after exposure to a pathogen in order to prevent the infection from occurring.

academic procrastination.text: Procrastination is an avoidance coping behavior that involves unnecessarily delaying or postponing something despite knowing that there could be negative consequences for doing so.

emergency severity index.text: The Emergency Severity Index (ESI) is a five-level emergency department triage algorithm, initially developed in 1998 by emergency physicians Richard Wurez and David Eitel, along with emergency nurses Nicki Gilboy, Taula Tanabe, and Debbie Travers.

inverse reinforcement learning.text: In machine learning and optimal control, reinforcement learning (RL) is concerned with how an intelligent agent should take actions in a dynamic environment in order to maximize a reward signal.

dental calculus.text: In dentistry, dental calculus or tartar is a form of hardened dental plaque.

deep learning.text: In machine learning, deep learning (DL) focuses on utilizing multilayered neural networks to perform tasks such as classification, regression, and representation learning.

causal inference.text: Causal inference is the process of determining the independent, actual effect of a particular phenomenon that is a component of a larger system.

weight stigma.text: Social stigma of obesity is bias or discriminatory behaviors targeted at overweight and obese individuals because of their weight and high body fat percentage.

latent profile analysis.text: In statistics, a mixture model is a probabilistic model for representing the presence of subpopulations within an overall population, without requiring that an observed data set should identify the sub-population to which an individual observation belongs.

cam plants.text: Crassulacean acid metabolism, also known as CAM photosynthesis, is a carbon fixation pathway that evolved in some plants as an adaptation to arid conditions that allows a plant to photosynthesize during the day, but only exchange gases at night.

metabolism.text: Metabolism refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.

hormone therapy.text: Hormone therapy or hormonal therapy is the use of hormones in medical treatment.

renewable energy.text: Renewable energy is energy made from renewable natural resources that are replenished on a human timescale.

privacy.text: Privacy is the ability of an individual or group to seclude themselves or information about themselves, and thereby express themselves selectively.

antarctica.text: Antarctica is Earth's southernmost and least-populated continent.

quantum computer.text: A quantum computer is a computer that represents and processes information using quantum states.

grade.text: The GRADE approach is a method of assessing the certainty in evidence and the strength of recommendations in health care.

alpha-lactalbumin.text: α-lactalbumin, also known as alpha-lactalbumin and LALBA, is a protein that in humans is encoded by the LALBA gene.

tryptophan.text: Tryptophan (symbol Trp or W), historically also known as tryptophane, is an α-amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

heterogeneity.text: Homogeneity and heterogeneity are concepts relating to the uniformity of a substance, process or image.

publication bias.text: In published academic research, publication bias occurs when the outcome of an experiment or research study biases the decision to publish or otherwise distribute it.

informal carer.text: A caregiver, caretaker or direct care worker is a person who provides physical, emotional or personal care for people who can not function independently due to age, chronic illness, injury or disability.

neglected tropical diseases.text: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) are a diverse group of tropical infections that are common in low-income populations in developing regions of Africa, Asia, and the Americas.

randomised trial.text: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) is a type of statistical experiment designed to evaluate the efficacy or safety of an intervention by minimizing bias through the random allocation of participants to one or more comparison groups.

postpartum depression.text: Postpartum depression (PPD), from Latin post partum, also known as perinatal depression, is a mood disorder which may be experienced by pregnant or postpartum women.

post-training.text: Post-training of large language models is a term used in recent technical literature for training applied to a large language model (LLM) after its initial large-scale pretraining.

ensemble learning.text: In statistics and machine learning, ensemble methods use multiple learning algorithms to obtain better predictive performance than could be obtained from any of the constituent learning algorithms alone.

problematic internet use.text: Internet addiction disorder (IAD), also called problematic Internet use (PIU), is characterized by excessive or poorly controlled preoccupations, urges, or behaviors regarding computer use and Internet access that lead to impairment or distress.

cortisol.text: Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.

emotional memory.text: Emotion can have a powerful effect on humans and animals.

dopamine.text: Dopamine is a neuromodulatory molecule that plays several important roles in cells.

associative learning.text: Learning is the process of acquiring new understanding, knowledge, behavior, skills, values, attitudes, and preferences.

marine heat wave.text: A marine heatwave is a period of abnormally high sea surface temperatures (SST) compared to typical temperatures for a particular season and locale.

coral bleaching.text: Coral bleaching is the process where corals become white due to loss of symbiotic algae and photosynthetic pigments.

cervical cancer.text: Cervical cancer is a type of cancer that develops in the cervix, the lower narrow part of the uterus (womb).

brain.text: The brain is an organ that serves as the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate and most invertebrate animals.

machine-learning.text: Machine learning (ML) is a field of study in artificial intelligence concerned with the development and study of statistical algorithms that can learn from data and generalize to unseen data, and thus perform tasks without being explicitly programmed.

weather forecasting.text: Weather forecasting or weather prediction is the application of science and technology to predict the conditions of the atmosphere for a given location and time.

emergency planning.text: Disaster management is the systematic reduction of a community's vulnerability to natural and man-made hazards as well as the coordinated response to disasters after they occur.

mycorrhizal fungi.text: A mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a plant, in which fungal hyphae and plant roots become interconnected and form an interface on the cellular level.

soil health.text: Soil health is a state of a soil meeting its range of ecosystem functions as appropriate to its environment.

probiotics.text: Probiotics are live microorganisms that are intended to support or improve the health and wellbeing of a host organism.

items.title: Future in mind: Systematic review of compassion-based interventions in higher education and feasibility study of Compassionate Mind Training with pre-registration Mental Health Student Nurses
items.venue: Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)

ai.headline: Compassion-based training may be acceptable and feasible for student nurses, but more trials are needed.
ai.summary: A review of 33 studies involving 4,897 higher education students looked at how compassion-based interventions are recruited and delivered. A separate small feasibility study of Compassionate Mind Training with 38 first-year mental health student nurses found high acceptability and positive wellbeing measure responses, though it was not a randomised trial.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how student wellbeing support might be tested and improved in demanding courses like nursing.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing when you are self-critical and respond to yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend.
ai.fact: Compassion-based interventions are being studied as ways to prevent and address psychological problems in higher education students.

quiz.question: What did the feasibility study find about Compassionate Mind Training for student nurses?
quiz.answer: Participants rated it highly on enjoyableness, usefulness and clarity, and qualitative feedback indicated it was acceptable.

ai.caveat: The student nurse study was small, single-group and quasi-experimental, so it cannot prove the training caused the improvements.

items.title: Effects of dance-based physical activity on cognitive and psychological health across age groups: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Dance-based activity may help some thinking and mood outcomes, especially in older adults, but evidence is mixed.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 22 controlled trials with 1,645 people aged 4 to 94 looked at dance-based physical activity. It found some favourable links with global cognition, memory, attention, depression, anxiety, stress, well-being and quality of life, but results were inconsistent and executive function findings were mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows dance could be a low-cost way to support mental and cognitive health, though stronger evidence is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Try joining a regular dance or movement class to see if it helps your mood and focus.
ai.fact: Dance-based physical activity combines motor, cognitive, emotional and social elements.

quiz.question: What did the review find about executive function?
quiz.answer: Findings for executive function were mixed.

ai.caveat: Many studies had a high risk of bias, samples were small, and most evidence came from older adults, so firm conclusions cannot be drawn.

items.title: Effects of Active Video Games on Cardiometabolic Health in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

ai.headline: Active video games may slightly lower BMI and blood pressure in children and teens.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 14 randomised trials with 942 children and adolescents aged 4-18. Active video games were linked to small reductions in body mass index and systolic blood pressure, while effects on other heart and metabolism measures were uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that active video games can be a fun way to add movement and may support heart health in young people.
ai.life_skill: Try swapping some seated screen time for active video games that get you moving.
ai.fact: Active video games were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure in children and adolescents.

quiz.question: What did active video games reduce in children and adolescents according to the review?
quiz.answer: They were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure.

ai.caveat: The evidence is based on a limited number of trials and certainty for many outcomes remains uncertain.

items.title: The Role of Community Pharmacists in Identifying and Managing Insomnia and Facilitating Access to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) – a Systematic Review

ai.headline: Community pharmacists may help identify insomnia and guide people toward CBT-I, but this is not yet common practice.
ai.summary: A systematic review of nine studies looked at how community pharmacists manage chronic insomnia. It found pharmacists could spot insomnia during counselling, reduce inappropriate sleeping medicines, and signpost or deliver CBT-I, though standard protocols, referral routes and time are lacking.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows a possible way to get evidence-based sleep help more easily through a local pharmacy rather than only a GP or specialist.
ai.life_skill: If you struggle with sleep, ask your community pharmacist whether they can screen for insomnia or point you to CBT-I.
ai.fact: Insomnia affects approximately 10% of the global adult population.

quiz.question: What did the review find about community pharmacists and insomnia?
quiz.answer: They could identify insomnia, deprescribe inappropriate hypnotics, and in some settings deliver or signpost patients to CBT-I.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the included studies were limited by a lack of standardised protocols, referral pathways and time constraints.

items.title: Family Educational and Cultural Practices Amplify Rather than Buffer Socioeconomic Inequalities in Academic Achievement in France

ai.headline: Family educational practices may widen, not narrow, school achievement gaps linked to family background in France.
ai.summary: Researchers followed 12,904 French students from Grade 5 to Grade 9 and looked at family background and home educational practices such as cultural activities and parental involvement. Practices were linked to higher achievement overall, but when they made a difference they tended to help students from higher-background families more, reinforcing rather than reducing gaps.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that extra home support does not automatically close achievement gaps and can sometimes make them wider.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the extra educational activities you do at home are helping everyone equally or mainly those who already have advantages.
ai.fact: In this French study, family educational practices were generally more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds.

quiz.question: Did family educational practices mainly reduce or reinforce socioeconomic achievement gaps in this study?
quiz.answer: They tended to reinforce gaps by being more beneficial for students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that family practices cause the achievement patterns.

items.title: Engagement or disengagement: understanding the emotional dynamics of EFL learners in GenAI-assisted writing from the sociocultural perspective

ai.headline: Students' feelings about using AI for English writing change over time and differ from person to person.
ai.summary: Researchers followed three Chinese university students learning English as a foreign language over a 14-week course that used generative AI for writing tasks. They found three different emotional patterns: one student stayed mostly positive, one moved from practical disengagement to critical engagement, and one moved from moderate disengagement to a breakdown and stronger disengagement. These patterns were shaped by a mix of personal factors, such as English proficiency and AI literacy, and environmental factors, such as task design and teacher or peer support.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI tools do not affect every learner's emotions in the same way, so support needs to be tailored to individual students.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your own feelings change when you use AI for schoolwork and ask a teacher or peer for help if you become discouraged.
ai.fact: Emotional engagement with AI-assisted writing is a dynamic and fluid state that interacts with behavioural and cognitive engagement over time.

ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how new AI and data-sharing tools in banking can change who gets credit and at what price, potentially helping or harming people who are financially excluded.

items.title: Psychological Factors Associated with Function and Health-Related Quality of Life Outcomes following Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews.

ai.headline: Depression and anxiety are linked to worse recovery after hip or knee replacement, while positive expectations may help.
ai.summary: This umbrella review combined 25 systematic reviews covering 40,024 patients who had total hip or knee replacement surgery. It found that depression and anxiety are linked to poorer function and quality of life after both operations, while distress, fear of movement, pain catastrophising and pessimism were linked to worse results after knee replacement only. Patient expectations and mental well-being were linked to better outcomes after knee replacement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how someone feels before joint surgery can be linked to how well they recover, so emotional health matters alongside physical health.

ai.caveat: This is an umbrella review of observational prognostic evidence (Level III), so it shows links rather than proving that psychological factors cause the outcomes.

items.title: State violence, protest suppression, and trauma outcomes: a scoping review of cumulative exposure across different political contexts

ai.headline: State violence against protesters is linked to trauma symptoms that can spread beyond those directly attacked.
ai.summary: This scoping review mapped research from 2016 to 2026 on how state suppression of protests affects mental health across six exposure settings. It found associations between protest suppression and post-traumatic stress symptoms, depression, anxiety, suicidality, and chronic hypervigilance, including among people not directly exposed to violence.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that political repression can harm mental health at a population level, not just among individuals directly involved in protests.
ai.life_skill: Notice how ongoing news or stories about political unrest affect your own mood and stress levels.
ai.fact: Psychological harm from protest suppression can extend beyond direct encounters with violence through cumulative insecurity, digital mediation, prolonged threat, and cross-border coercion.

quiz.question: According to the review, who can experience psychological harm from protest suppression?
quiz.answer: Harm is not limited to people directly exposed to violence and can extend through indirect, mediated, and transnational exposure.

ai.caveat: A scoping review maps existing evidence rather than proving cause and effect, and the included studies vary in design and how directly they measured mental health.

items.title: A quasi-experimental evaluation of one-to-one counselling to improve mental health and education outcomes amongst school pupils in England, Scotland and Wales

ai.headline: School counselling reduced mental health difficulties but did not improve school attendance.
ai.summary: Researchers compared about 15,000 pupils who received one-to-one school counselling with matched pupils who did not. Counselling was linked to greater reductions in mental health difficulties scores, but there was no evidence it improved attendance or reduced persistent absence.

ai.fact: One-to-one school counselling was linked to small but meaningful reductions in pupils’ mental health difficulty scores.

items.title: Adapting Non-Violent Resistance for Families of Young People with Complex Neurodevelopmental Needs: A Service Evaluation of Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Clinical Outcomes

ai.headline: An adapted eight-week parent group based on Non-Violent Resistance was feasible and acceptable for parents of young people with complex neurodevelopmental needs.
ai.summary: The study looked at a pilot Non-Violent Resistance parent group run by a specialist CAMHS team for ten parents of young people with learning disabilities and complex neurodevelopmental needs. items.title: Early wounds, minds in training: childhood adversity and the mediating effect of psychological distress in suicidal risk among medical students

ai.headline: Childhood maltreatment is linked to higher suicide risk among medical students, partly through depression, anxiety and academic stress.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 670 second-year medical students in Mexico about childhood maltreatment, mental health, academic stress and suicide risk. items.title: Effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative interventions for post-COVID-19 condition: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Supervised exercise rehab and CBT may help adults with post-COVID-19 condition improve fitness and reduce fatigue.

ai.why_it_matters: It points to non-drug options that may help people manage ongoing symptoms after COVID-19 and regain everyday function.
ai.life_skill: Try asking a qualified health professional about supervised rehabilitation or CBT if you have ongoing post-COVID symptoms.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Artificial Intelligence in Digital Learning: A Systematic Review of Federated Learning, Differential Privacy, Security, and Educational Utility in Higher Education

ai.headline: Privacy-protecting AI in university digital learning is promising but not yet proven in real institutions.

ai.fact: Federated learning was the most common privacy method studied, appearing in 15 of the 33 included studies.

ai.headline: Exercise programmes can improve physical, motor, cognitive and social health in people with Down syndrome.

items.title: Longitudinal associations between task-control network functioning, cognition, and the environment in early adolescence

ai.headline: Brain networks linked to focus grow alongside thinking skills and attention during early adolescence.

items.title: Effects of an embodied music intervention on executive function, emotion regulation and psychophysiological well-being in children: the role of movement-rhythm synchronization and self-regulation

ai.headline: Adding whole-body movement to music lessons improved children’s focus, emotion control and rhythm skills more than music alone.
ai.summary: A randomised trial assigned 180 children aged 8–11 to embodied music, non-embodied music, or usual activity for 12 weeks. items.title: Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints

ai.headline: AI agents learn best when they remember only what is worth reusing, not everything they experience.
ai.summary: The study looked at AI agents that keep learning after they are deployed while working under tight limits on memory and processing. It found that many advanced memory methods performed no better than simple retrieval or no memory at all when resources were scarce. A new method that learns which memories are actually worth keeping and reusing achieved the highest success rate while using the fewest output tokens.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that under tight limits, choosing what to keep matters more than storing more information, which applies to how people manage limited time, attention, and notes.
ai.life_skill: Try keeping only the information you are actually likely to use again, rather than saving everything.
ai.fact: Retrieving a relevant but ineffective memory can consume scarce resources and hinder downstream performance.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find matters most for AI agents working under tight memory limits?
quiz.answer: Learning which experiences are worth retaining and reusing, rather than simply remembering more.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings come from simulated AI agent environments rather than real people.

items.title: Development and Characterization of Herbal Tea Supplemented with Beetroot

ai.headline: Researchers developed a beetroot herbal tea powder that scored highest for antioxidants and minerals among four blends tested.
ai.summary: The study created instant herbal tea powders using hibiscus, beetroot, lemon peel and anhydrous honey in different ratios. The blend with 45% beetroot and 45% hibiscus (T3) had the highest iron, calcium, potassium, phenolic content, flavonoids and antioxidant activity, and was rated most acceptable by consumers.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how common ingredients can be combined into a tea that is rich in nutrients linked to fighting oxidative stress.

quiz.question: Which treatment had the highest mineral and antioxidant results?

items.title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis

ai.headline: AI can help doctors tell two serious heart conditions apart from an ECG, especially with visual explanations.
ai.summary: Researchers trained deep-learning models on ECG images to distinguish Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior heart attack. In a reader study, healthcare providers became much more accurate when using AI assistance, and adding heatmap explanations helped further.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI tools might support faster, more accurate interpretation of heart tests in everyday healthcare.

ai.summary: Scientists found that small cancer cells carrying extra chromosomes can grow faster, spread more easily, and resist common treatments compared to larger cells. This discovery might help explain why some tumors are particularly dangerous and offer a new way to predict patient outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that the physical size of a cell is not always the best indicator of how dangerous a disease might be.
ai.fact: Small cancer cells with extra chromosomes are linked to faster growth and greater resistance to treatment.

quiz.question: According to the report, what characteristic makes small cancer cells more dangerous?
quiz.answer: They carry extra chromosomes, which allows them to grow faster and resist treatments.

ai.caveat: This is a news summary of a discovery, not a peer-reviewed study, so the specific mechanisms and clinical applications are not yet fully established.

ai.summary: Researchers studied intimate partner violence reporting using different data collection methods. items.title: VLA-Δ: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models

ai.headline: New framework improves robot control
ai.summary: Researchers studied vision-language-action models for robot control, proposing a new framework called VLA-Δ, which uses physical state transitions as learning targets. This framework achieves competitive performance on benchmarks and outperforms other methods in real-robot experiments. The model generates actions directly from current observations without additional inference overhead.
ai.why_it_matters: This research matters because it could lead to more efficient and effective robot control in various applications, such as manufacturing and healthcare.
ai.life_skill: Try to understand how machines learn from their environment
ai.fact: Vision-language-action models can transfer semantic knowledge to robot control

quiz.question: What is the main goal of the VLA-Δ framework?

items.title: Separable downmodulation of meiotic axis protein deposition and DNA break induction at chromosome ends

ai.headline: Yeast cells use several overlapping mechanisms to stop DNA breaks near chromosome ends during meiosis.
ai.summary: The study looked at how yeast cells limit recombination proteins and DNA breaks near telomeres. It found multiple, often chromosome-specific mechanisms work together, including Dot1 and Sir proteins, to keep these regions quiet.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how cells protect chromosome ends during cell division, helping us understand how genetic stability is maintained.
ai.fact: Multiple overlapping mechanisms suppress DNA double-strand breaks within 20 kb of telomeres in yeast meiosis.

quiz.question: What did the study find about DNA break suppression near chromosome ends?
quiz.answer: Multiple, often chromosome-specific mechanisms contribute to the low levels of DNA breaks near telomeres.

ai.caveat: This is a single lab study in yeast, so the findings may not apply to humans or other organisms.

items.title: Mapping Global Pain and Trauma: A Seven-Domain Framework and the Fundamental Peace Index for the Journey from Shadow to Fundamental Peace

ai.headline: A new seven-domain map scores countries’ pain and trauma, but it is still an untested hypothesis.
ai.summary: The paper proposes the Global Pain and Trauma Map, a seven-domain framework covering psychological, relational, cultural, structural, existential, somatic and environmental suffering, plus a Fundamental Peace Index equal to 100 minus the pain score. Across 196 countries, the average pain score was 59.1 out of 100, meaning an average Fundamental Peace score of 40.9, though the scores are expert estimates rather than direct measurements.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how researchers are trying to bring together different kinds of suffering—from loneliness to ecological grief—into one shared framework for policy and understanding.
ai.life_skill: Notice which areas of your life feel most strained, such as relationships, work, health or environment, and consider where support might help.
ai.fact: Roughly seven in ten adults worldwide experience at least one traumatic event in their lifetime.

quiz.question: What is the Fundamental Peace Index based on?
quiz.answer: It is calculated as 100 minus the Global Pain and Trauma Map composite score.

ai.caveat: The country scores are expert-rated estimates, not direct measurements, and the framework is described as a structured hypothesis awaiting validation.

items.title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Iron Overload Disorders: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis of Bioenergetic Dysfunction, Oxidative Stress, and Biomarker-Guided Management.

ai.headline: Iron chelation lowers iron overload, but newer cell-injury markers still need proof before routine use.
ai.summary: The review looked at studies of iron chelation therapy for people with transfusion-dependent iron overload. It found chelation drugs consistently reduce systemic iron burden and may reduce mitochondrial damage, oxidative stress and ferroptotic cell death in preclinical models, but these newer biomarkers are not yet validated for routine clinical use.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how doctors track and treat dangerous iron buildup, and why promising new blood tests still need more evidence before they guide everyday care.
ai.life_skill: If you or someone you know has iron overload, discuss monitoring and treatment options with a qualified specialist rather than relying on new biomarker tests alone.
ai.fact: Iron overload from repeated transfusions is linked to oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptotic cell death.

quiz.question: What did the review conclude about newer biomarkers of mitochondrial injury, oxidative stress and ferroptosis?
quiz.answer: They provide promising mechanistic insights but their clinical utility remains uncertain because of limited prospective validation and insufficient standardization.

ai.caveat: The included studies were heterogeneous and many were preclinical, so the findings about cellular mechanisms are not yet proven in routine clinical practice.

ai.headline: French priest's view of 17th century Iran
ai.summary: A French priest's travelogue was studied to examine cultural aspects of 17th century Iran. The book portrays various aspects of Iranian life, including religion and customs. The research analyzed the priest's perspective on Iranian culture.

ai.headline: Mental health support helps in Nepal
ai.summary: The PARBARDHAN project used a community-based approach to support mental health in Nepal. The project's endline evaluation found lower anxiety and depression, but higher psychological distress. Qualitative findings indicated increased mental health awareness and support

items.title: Generative AI-Driven Feedback in Flipped Writing Workshops: Transforming Business Education through Improved Writing, Communication, and Self-Regulation

ai.headline: AI feedback in flipped writing workshops improved students’ writing, communication and self-regulation over 14 weeks.
ai.summary: A study compared 113 business students who used AI-driven feedback in flipped workshops with 81 students in traditional lectures. The AI group showed higher analytical writing scores, better professional communication, and more revision cycles and goal-setting than the control group.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI tools might help people practise writing and self-directed learning outside the classroom.
ai.life_skill: Try using AI feedback to revise your writing and set specific goals before checking your work again.
ai.fact: Students using AI-driven feedback in flipped workshops completed more revision cycles than students in traditional lectures.

quiz.question: What did students using AI-driven feedback do more of compared with the control group?
quiz.answer: They completed more revision cycles and set more precise goals.

ai.caveat: It is one study in business education, so the results may not apply to all learners or settings.

items.title: Professional Identity and Its Influencing Factors Among Nursing Interns: The Mediating Role of Career Adaptability Between Social Support and Professional Identity

ai.headline: Social support and career adaptability are linked to stronger professional identity in nursing interns.
ai.summary: A study of 407 nursing interns in China looked at what affects their professional identity. It found that higher social support and career adaptability were linked to stronger professional identity, while higher perceived stress was linked to weaker identity; career adaptability partly explained how social support helped.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how support networks and adaptable career thinking may help new health workers feel they belong in their profession.
ai.life_skill: Notice what support and flexible career thinking help you feel more confident in a new job or training role.
ai.fact: In this study, professional identity was significantly positively correlated with social support (r=0.474), psychological resilience (r=0.389), and career adaptability (r=0.609), and negatively correlated with perceived stress (r=-0.378).

quiz.question: What did the study find about career adaptability and social support in relation to professional identity?
quiz.answer: Both were significant positive predictors of professional identity, and career adaptability partly mediated the link between social support and professional identity.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and used convenience sampling at one hospital, so the results are preliminary and may not apply more widely.

ai.summary: Researchers studied a framework called CoDA to improve robot training through simulation. They found that CoDA improved out-of-distribution success in manipulation tasks. The framework co-evolves a simulation data engine and an action policy to address policy failures.

ai.headline: European school policies rarely treat religious-based bullying as a separate issue.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed 63 education policy documents from nine European countries. They found most countries address religion within general equality, diversity and anti-bullying frameworks, with only Cyprus explicitly naming religious-based bullying.

ai.fact: Religious-based bullying targets people because of their religious beliefs, practices or visible religious identity.

quiz.answer: Most addressed it within broader equality, diversity and inclusion or anti-bullying frameworks rather than as a distinct concern.

items.title: Early Prototyping and Usability Testing (ACPS)

ai.headline: Researchers are testing a personalised mobile app to help young people with chronic conditions take their medication.
ai.summary: This pilot trial is refining a mobile health intervention for adolescents and young adults with chronic health conditions. It compares an adaptive intervention that personalises support intensity against automated text message reminders to see which better promotes medication adherence.

items.title: Positive error-handling in TGfU-based basketball instruction: effects on tactical decision-making and the role of perceived classroom psychological safety

ai.headline: Positive error-handling in basketball lessons improved tactical decisions and was linked to greater psychological safety.
ai.summary: Sixty students were randomly assigned to two eight-week basketball classes using the same TGfU teaching approach, one with positive error-handling and one with neutral error-handling. The positive error-handling group showed larger gains in tactical decision-making that were retained three weeks later, and their psychological safety increased more than the neutral group's.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that how teachers respond to mistakes may matter for learning in games-based PE and possibly other classroom settings.
ai.life_skill: Try treating mistakes in practice as useful information rather than something to avoid or hide.
ai.fact: Positive error-handling was associated with larger improvements in tactical decision-making and psychological safety compared with neutral error-handling.

quiz.question: What did the study find about psychological safety in the positive error-handling class compared with the neutral class?
quiz.answer: Psychological safety increased more in the positive error-handling class, while the increase in the neutral class was not statistically significant.

ai.caveat: There was only one class per condition, so classroom-specific influences could not be separated from the teaching condition, and statistics were not adjusted for within-class dependence.

ai.headline: New method studies chromosomal instability
ai.summary: Researchers developed a rapid method to study micronuclei, which are linked to chromosomal instability. They used this method to explore the features of micronuclei in cells and cancer models. The method allows for simple and rapid purification of micronuclei from various sources.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding chromosomal instability is important for understanding cancer development and progression.
ai.fact: Micronuclei are extra-nuclear structures formed following aberrant chromosome mis-segregation.

ai.summary: Researchers looked at why changing eating habits is difficult. They found that existing feelings about food, such as disliking olives or loving pastries, may interfere with learning new eating habits.

ai.headline: Brain areas cleared of amyloid plaques showed much less harmful tau buildup than nearby damaged areas.
ai.summary: Researchers examined the brain of one person with Alzheimer’s disease. They found that regions where amyloid plaques had been removed had very little tau buildup, while neighbouring areas showed extensive damage.

items.title: How Knowledge Crosses Borders: Evidence from Semiconductor Manufacturing -- by Pinelopi K. Goldberg, Réka Juhász, Giulia Lo Forte, Jeff Thurk

ai.headline: Knowledge in chip manufacturing spreads through business links, not automatically across borders.
ai.summary: The study looks at how knowledge moves between countries in semiconductor manufacturing. It finds that learning happens through supply chains, engineers moving between firms, and foreign investment, rather than spreading freely on its own.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that access to advanced technology depends on international business relationships, not just geography or time.
ai.life_skill: Notice how skills and ideas often travel through the people and companies you work with, not just through public information.
ai.fact: Cross-border learning in semiconductor manufacturing is linked to market mechanisms such as supply chains, engineer mobility, and foreign direct investment.

quiz.question: How does the study say knowledge mainly crosses borders in chip manufacturing?
quiz.answer: Through purposeful economic relationships like supply chains, engineer movement, and foreign investment, rather than automatic spillovers.

ai.caveat: This is an NBER working paper that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are preliminary.

items.title: Global systematic review of how climate change degrades the wellbeing and health of Indigenous children.

ai.headline: Climate change is linked to poorer health and wellbeing among Indigenous children worldwide.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 53 studies found that climate change is linked to adverse health outcomes in Indigenous children, including effects on psychosocial and cultural wellbeing, malnutrition, infectious diseases, perinatal health, and morbidity and mortality. Heat exposure and seasonal and hydroclimatic variability were the most frequently reported climate exposures.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how environmental changes can affect the health and cultural wellbeing of children in Indigenous communities around the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how changes in weather and seasons affect your own mood, energy, and daily routines.
ai.fact: Indigenous children across diverse global contexts are experiencing adverse climate-related health outcomes.

quiz.question: What were the most frequently linked climate exposures in the review?
quiz.answer: Heat exposure and seasonal and hydroclimatic variability were the most frequently linked climate exposures.

ai.caveat: The studies were heterogeneous and meta-analysis was not feasible, so findings are narrative rather than pooled statistics.

items.title: Education and training interventions for healthcare workers to prevent sexual harassment.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Training may slightly improve knowledge and skills for preventing sexual harassment among healthcare workers.
ai.summary: This Cochrane review looked at education and training to prevent sexual harassment in healthcare settings. Two studies involving 170 nurses found that training probably slightly increases prevention knowledge and may slightly improve management skills, but no study measured whether harassment actually decreased.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that while training can build awareness, there is no evidence yet that it stops harassment from happening.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether workplace training actually changes behaviour, not just what people know.
ai.fact: Sexual harassment among healthcare workers is linked to poor mental health, job dissatisfaction, and people leaving their jobs.

quiz.question: Did the review find evidence that training reduces the incidence of sexual harassment?
quiz.answer: No, none of the included studies measured the incidence of sexual harassment.

ai.caveat: The review is based on only two small studies of nurses in Taiwan, and both compared different types of training rather than training versus no training.

items.title: Pre-sleep alpha-lactalbumin and dietary protein interactions on sleep, mood, and cognition in athletes with sleep difficulties: a protocol for a factorial crossover randomised controlled trial

ai.headline: A trial will test whether a milk protein supplement improves sleep, mood and thinking in athletes who sleep poorly.
ai.summary: This study protocol describes a planned randomised crossover trial in 24 athletes with sleep difficulties. It will compare alpha-lactalbumin, a whey protein from cow’s milk, with a placebo under two different dietary protein conditions, measuring sleep, mood and cognition.
ai.why_it_matters: It could show whether a simple whole-food supplement helps athletes sleep better and recover more effectively.

quiz.question: What is the main aim of the planned trial?
quiz.answer: To investigate whether alpha-lactalbumin supplementation improves sleep, mood and cognition in athletes with sleep difficulties.

ai.caveat: This is only a study protocol, so no results have been collected or analysed yet.

items.title: A Critical Epistemological Audit of Early Evidence Syntheses in Generative AI Educational Research: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

ai.headline: Early reviews of ChatGPT in education show mixed, uncertain results because the underlying studies vary widely in quality.
ai.summary: Researchers audited five early meta-analyses covering 87 studies on ChatGPT’s effects in education. They found a positive average effect, but results varied greatly and weakened when stricter quality checks were applied, especially for studies measuring actual learning rather than performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why a single headline number about AI in education should not be taken as proof of a stable, general benefit.
ai.life_skill: Check whether claims about educational tools are based on high-quality, transparent research before relying on them.
ai.fact: Most early studies assessed performance exclusively, while only a small share assessed learning exclusively.

quiz.question: What did the reconstructed meta-analysis find about the average effect of ChatGPT on educational outcomes?
quiz.answer: It found a positive average effect, but the results varied substantially and became weaker under stricter quality checks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Informal carers’ experiences of mental health services regarding supporting those they care for and getting support for their own wellbeing: A systematic umbrella review of qualitative evidence

ai.headline: Informal carers often face exclusion, distress and barriers when using mental health services for themselves or the person they support.
ai.summary: This umbrella review combined findings from twelve qualitative reviews about unpaid carers’ experiences of mental health services. It found that while some carers had positive experiences, most described exclusion, emotional distress and structural barriers to getting support for themselves or the person they care for.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how mental health services can affect not only service users but also the family and friends who support them.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether services are involving and supporting you as a carer, and ask for information about carer support if you are not being included.
ai.fact: Informal carers include family members, friends or other unpaid supporters of people with mental health difficulties.

quiz.question: What did most carers describe in their experiences of mental health services?
quiz.answer: Most described exclusion, emotional distress and structural barriers to support.

ai.caveat: The findings come from qualitative reviews of carers’ experiences, so they show patterns of reported experience rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: The psychosocial impacts of skin-neglected tropical diseases (SNTDs) as perceived by the affected persons: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Skin neglected tropical diseases cause serious mental and social harm, especially for women.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 27 qualitative studies on people living with skin neglected tropical diseases such as leprosy and cutaneous leishmaniasis. Most participants reported stigma, avoidance, abandonment, low mood, anxiety and reduced ability to work or socialise, with women generally facing worse social consequences.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how visible illness can damage mental health and social participation, highlighting the need for supportive communities and early treatment.
ai.life_skill: Notice if someone with a visible skin condition is being avoided and offer ordinary, respectful contact.
ai.fact: Skin neglected tropical diseases are linked to stigma, low mood, anxiety and reduced social participation.

quiz.question: Which group generally experienced worse social consequences from skin neglected tropical diseases?
quiz.answer: Women generally experienced worse social consequences than men.

ai.caveat: The review only included qualitative studies published in English, so findings may not apply to all settings or languages.

items.title: Human-Centered GenAI Feedback Design in Higher Education: A Multisite Experiment on Direct, Reflective, and Hybrid Approaches to Scientific Argumentation
items.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

ai.headline: GenAI feedback works best when students stay in charge of their own learning
ai.summary: A multisite experiment with 1,176 first-year science students compared peer-only, direct AI, reflective AI, and hybrid feedback. Direct AI feedback improved argument quality most quickly, but reflective and hybrid designs led to better uptake, self-regulated learning, conceptual learning, and delayed AI-free transfer.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how AI feedback is designed matters more than simply having access to AI, especially for lasting learning.
ai.life_skill: When using AI feedback, pause to judge and revise the work yourself rather than just accepting the AI's suggestions.
ai.fact: Feedback designs that preserve student agency and evaluative judgment can support better delayed learning than direct AI feedback alone.

quiz.question: Which feedback condition showed the clearest advantage on conceptual learning?
quiz.answer: The hybrid condition combining self-evaluation, peer feedback, and GenAI critique yielded the highest adjusted mean for immediate argument-quality gain and showed the clearest advantage on conceptual learning.
